identity.resolvedIdentity: The Borgarsyssel Museum open-air museum and immediate St. Nikolas ruin-park interpretation complex, used as the physical gateway to the wider medieval city Borg and Olav tradition.
identity.identityProblem: The record combines a present museum destination with the wider and partly lost medieval city. A physical anchor can represent the museum and ruins but not an invented centre for the whole city or landslide area.
identity.splitReason: The museum and ruin park form one coherent visitor and interpretation complex. The medieval city remains wider historical context.

requiredEvidence: explicit separation from the full medieval city and landslide scar

evidence.finding: The named museum area has a representative point at 59.27874, 11.12367 and is linked to Wikidata Q4945018 and SSR place-name number 83087.
evidence.reason: Directly represents the museum and immediate outdoor complex.

evidence.finding: The official museum describes an open-air museum with 25 buildings, Olavs hall, a tower, St. Nikolas church ruins and interpretation of the medieval city Borg.
The official visitor and postal address is Gamlebygata 8, 1721 Sarpsborg.
The published coordinate 59.27879, 11.12404 lies approximately 21.7 metres from the applied point.
The official description distinguishes the museum and church ruins from the 1702 landslide scar where much of the medieval city lay.
evidence.reason: Prevents the museum point from being misrepresented as the full medieval-city geometry.

evidence.finding: The legacy point lies approximately 825.8 metres northwest of the museum area.
evidence.reason: Replaced because it does not represent the museum, ruins or immediate Olavsbyen complex.
